title: Finite lying-over for normalization, with the completed-branch bound
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every prime ideal $p\subset R$, the set $\{Q\subset N:Q\text{ is prime and }Q\cap R=p\}$ is finite. More precisely, its cardinality is at most the number of minimal prime ideals of $\widehat{R_p}$, the completion of $R_p$ at its maximal ideal $pR_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. A minimal prime means a prime minimal among all prime ideals.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Proposition 4.8.2, printed pp. 83-84 (PDF pp. 97-98), domain and own-fraction-field case, including the completed-branch bound. This is the independent finite-lying-over proof, not Heinzer’s later Noetherian-spectrum conclusion. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a prime $p\subset R$ and put $S=R\setminus p$, $A=S^{-1}R=R_p$, $m=pA$, and $B=S^{-1}N\subset K$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A$ is local with maximal ideal $m$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], applied to $R$ and $S$. Since $A\subset K$ contains $R$, it is a domain and its fraction field is $K$: every $a/d\in K$, with $a,d\in R$ and $d\ne0$, is already a quotient of elements of $A$. Every element of $S$ is a unit in $K$, so $S^{-1}K=K$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] to $R\to K$ shows that $B$ is exactly the integral closure of $A$ in $K$.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); local reduction of Swanson–Huneke Proposition 4.8.2, printed p. 84.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] to the localization $N\to S^{-1}N=B$, with $S$ viewed in $N$. It gives inverse extension and contraction on primes disjoint from $S$. Restrict these inverse maps to primes $Q\subset N$ with $Q\cap R=p$ and primes $q\subset B$ with $q\cap A=m$. This restriction is valid: $Q\cap R=p$ implies $Q\cap S=\varnothing$, and $a/s\in(QB)\cap A$ if and only if $a\in p$, since $s$ is a unit in $B$ and $(QB)\cap N=Q$. Conversely, $q\cap A=m$ gives $(q\cap N)\cap R=p$, because $a/1\in m$ is equivalent to $a\in p$. Thus the two prime sets have the same cardinality. It remains to bound the latter set for the Noetherian local domain $A$.

source.place: Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), restricted to the specified fibre; Swanson–Huneke Proposition 4.8.2, printed p. 84, localization paragraph.

proof.text: Put $H=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}A/m^n$ and let $n=\ker(H\to A/m)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $H$ is local with maximal ideal $n=mH$ and the contraction of $n$ to $A$ is $m$. Apply [lem-trf-normalization-completed-product-comparison] to $A$, $K$ and $B$. List the distinct minimal primes of $H$ as $h_1,\ldots,h_r$; the list is finite. In that node's notation put $C_i=H/h_i$, $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(C_i)$ and let $T_i$ be the integral closure of $C_i$ in $L_i$. Each $C_i$ is a complete Noetherian local domain. Its maximal ideal is $n_i=n/h_i$, since its quotient by $n/h_i$ is the field $H/n$ and every proper ideal is contained in the image of $n$. The same node supplies the embedding $e_i:K\hookrightarrow L_i$ induced by $A\hookrightarrow C_i$; its integrality assertion shows that $e_i(B)\subseteq T_i$. Write $j_i:B\to T_i$ for this restriction.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.2, printed p. 84, completed-component construction; Proposition 4.7.3 for component embeddings. Local completion: Stacks Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and 05GI (lemma-radical-completion).

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] applied to the $n_i$-adically complete $C_i$ makes $(C_i,n_i)$ henselian, so $C_i$ is henselian local by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The ring $T_i\subset L_i$ is nonzero and integral over $C_i$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Its only idempotents are $0$ and $1$, since $e(e-1)=0$ in a domain has these two solutions. Consequently [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] says that $T_i$ is local and $C_i\to T_i$ is local. Denote its unique maximal ideal by $M_i$; its contraction is $n_i$. Moreover every prime $M\subset T_i$ contracting to $n_i$ is maximal: $T_i/M$ is an integral domain integral over the field $C_i/n_i$. For $0\ne x$ in that domain choose a monic relation of least degree; its constant coefficient is nonzero, as otherwise cancellation of $x$ lowers the degree. Solving the relation for $x^{-1}$ proves that $T_i/M$ is a field. Hence every such $M$ equals $M_i$.

source.place: Tags 0ALJ (lemma-complete-henselian) and 092X (lemma-integral-over-henselian), domain case of the cited connected-integral-algebra node; this supplies the locality used from Swanson–Huneke Theorem 4.3.4 in Proposition 4.8.2.

proof.text: Let $q\subset B$ be any prime with $q\cap A=m$. Apply [lem-trf-normalization-completed-branch-lift] to the Noetherian local domain $A$ and its normalization $B\subset K$. It gives a minimal prime $h\subset H$, an $A$-algebra map $j:B\to T$ for the normalization $T$ of $H/h$ in its fraction field, and a prime $M\subset T$ with $j^{-1}(M)=q$ and contraction $n/h$ in $H/h$. Our list exhausts the minimal primes, so $h=h_i$ for some $i$ and $T=T_i$. Step 4 gives $M=M_i$. We must also identify the supplied map $j$ with the fixed $j_i$. For $b\in B\subset K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ write $b=a/d$ with $a,d\in A$, $d\ne0$. Inside $B$ we have $db=a$. Both $A$-algebra maps into $T_i\subset L_i$ therefore send $b$ to the same fraction $\bar a/\bar d$. The denominator is nonzero because the embedding $A\hookrightarrow C_i$ is injective by [lem-trf-normalization-completed-product-comparison]. Thus $j=j_i$, and $q=j_i^{-1}(M_i)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.8.3, printed p. 84, component form; Proposition 4.7.3 for injectivity on the base. The uniqueness calculation in the fraction field identifies the map in the lifting statement with the fixed component embedding.

proof.text: The preceding step shows that every prime of $B$ contracting to $m$ is one of the $r$ ideals $j_i^{-1}(M_i)$. These are primes, and each contracts to $m$: contraction along $C_i\to T_i$ gives $n_i$, along $H\to C_i$ gives $n$, and along $A\to H$ gives $m$. Some of the $r$ ideals may coincide; their image is nevertheless finite with cardinality at most $r$. By Step 2 the original fibre over $p$ has the same cardinality. Finally $H$ is exactly $\widehat{R_p}$, and $r$ is the number of all its minimal primes, so this is the claimed bound as well as finiteness. This argument includes $p=0$: then $A=K$, $H=K$, $r=1$ and the only fibre prime is $0$.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.2, completed-branch cardinality conclusion; elementary finite-image counting from the preceding steps.
